_README.what: Golden vectors harvested from third-party published worked examples, fetched 2026-07-29. Every expectedReturnMinor is a figure STATED BY THE SOURCE and quoted verbatim in sourceQuote. None was computed here — that is the entire point of this file.
_README.why: These grade the settlement engine. A fixture whose expected value came from the same understanding that wrote settle() grades nothing.
_README.units: All money is GBP pence as strings (docs/08 D1). £10 = "1000".
_README.odds: oddsTaken is decimal, converted from the fractional price the source states. oddsStated preserves the source's own wording. Converting a stated input's representation is not computing an expected value.
_README.raceParams: Where a source states place terms but not a runner count, race.actualRunners and race.isHandicap are set to a configuration consistent with the stated terms, and statedTerms records what the source actually said. Where the two could disagree, statedTerms wins.
_README.disputed: expectedDisputed:true means the SOURCE's stated figure is believed wrong, not that our engine is. Per docs/08 D15 these are excluded from the pass/fail gate but stay visible in the report. loadPublishedVectors() returns them in `disputed`, never in `graded`.
_README.sourceClass: THIRD-PARTY GUIDES, NOT BOOKMAKERS. All sixteen bookmaker fetches were blocked — docs/sources/BLOCKED-bookmakers.txt. Two of the six sources publish deduction tables that are provably wrong (docs/sources/COMPARISON.md §4); their worked examples are used, their tables are not.
_README.notGraded: This file does not replace races.json. It contains no real races, no finishing fields, no dead-heat-for-final-place, no non-runner-changes-band cases. It is a smoke test built from arithmetic other people published, not the 200-race regression suite tests/golden/README.md requires.
_README.rule4Input: Per docs/08 D14 the Rule 4 lookup input is a FRACTION. Each Rule 4 vector carries race.withdrawnAtFraction as {num,den} where the source states a fractional price. A vector whose source states only a decimal that is not on the ladder would be unsettleable, and none of the 27 is in that state — see the audit in the session report.
_README.d16Gap: docs/08 D16 — Rule 4 applies to BOTH parts of an each-way bet — is NOT covered here. All 7 Rule 4 vectors are win singles; all 11 each-way vectors are on races with no withdrawal. The intersection is empty, so D16 changes the expected settlement of ZERO of these 27 and conflicts with no source quote. It is also therefore unverified by fixture. loader.ts vectorsCoveringD16() is a tripwire on the gap.

vectors.sourceQuote: a 5p rule 4 deduction on a £100 stake on a 10/1 winner will reduce your profit by 5%. The profit on this bet would ordinarily be £1,000 so 5% of that is £50 - that's the deduction. The total return on the bet would be £1,050.

If you staked £10 on a horse at 6/1 and the Rule 4 deduction is 25p, your gross profit was £60. The deduction is £60 x 0.25 = £15. Your adjusted profit is £45, and your total return is £55 (£45 plus your £10 stake).

You have backed a winner at 4/1. Before the off, the 2/1 favourite is withdrawn at the start. The Tattersalls Rule 4 scale dictates that a withdrawal at 2/1 triggers a deduction of 30 pence in the pound of winnings. Your £10 winning stake would, without any deduction, pay £40 in winnings (plus the £10 stake back, total £50). The deduction of 30p in the pound takes 30% off the £40 of winnings - £12. Adjusted winnings are £28, total return £38.
vectors.note: Doubles as band evidence: 2/1 sits in 9/5-9/4, which the four-source table puts at 30p and the OLD docs/05 §5.1 put at 35p. This example agrees with the new table. Its source's own deduction table is discarded as unreliable — the example is not.

vectors.sourceQuote: You place a £20 win bet on Horse A at 4/1. Before the race, Horse B - the 6/4 joint-favourite - is withdrawn...a 40p deduction...winnings would be £80...£80 x 0.40 = £32. Your adjusted winnings are £80 minus £32, which equals £48. Add your £20 stake back, and the total return is £68 instead of £100.
vectors.note: Band evidence: 6/4 sits in 5/4-6/4, four sources say 40p, old docs/05 said 45p. Agrees with the new table.

vectors.sourceQuote: Same bet - £20 on Horse A at 4/1 - but this time the withdrawn horse was a 12/1 outsider...5p...Your winnings are still £80. The deduction: £80 x 0.05 = £4. Adjusted winnings: £76. Total return with stake: £96.
vectors.note: Exercises the smallest non-zero band, which docs/05 §5.1 flags as possibly operator-specific.

vectors.sourceQuote: Two horses are withdrawn...Horse B was priced at 3/1 (25p deduction) and Horse C at 5/1 (15p deduction...deductions stack: 25p + 15p = 40p...£80 x 0.40 = £32. Adjusted winnings: £48. Total return: £68.
vectors.note: MULTIPLE WITHDRAWALS. Confirms docs/05 §5.2 rule 2 — deductions add before being applied, they are not applied in sequence. Applying 25p then 15p to the remainder would give £51, not £48.

vectors.sourceQuote: If you stake £10 at 6.0 (5/1) and a 3.0 non-runner triggers a 30p Rule 4, your winnings of £50 are cut by 30%: £15 comes off, you receive £35 winnings + £10 stake = £45.
vectors.note: Source's own table is discarded (docs/sources/COMPARISON.md §4); this example is retained and agrees with the four-source table at 3.0 → 30p. D14 NOTE: this source states the withdrawn price as decimal 3.0 only. 3.0 is an exact ladder match for 2/1, so it snaps and settles. Had the source said 2.32 or 3.30, this vector would be unsettleable and would have to be dropped.

vectors.sourceQuote: £5 EW (total £10). Horse wins. Win part: £5 @ 10/1 -> return £55. Place part: £5 @ 2/1 -> return £15. Total return £70
Same bet; horse finishes 2nd. Win part loses. Place part: £15 return. Total return £15
vectors.note: The win half loses and the place half wins — the PARTIAL settlement path.

vectors.sourceQuote: Horse finishes outside places. Both parts lose; return £0.
Win part: £5 @ 10/1 -> return £55
vectors.note: The win half of the each-way example, stated as its own return. Two sources state the identical figure.

vectors.sourceQuote: Place part: £5 @ 2/1 -> return £15
vectors.note: Pins the place-fraction arithmetic: 1/5 of 10/1 is 2/1, NOT 11.0 x 0.2. docs/05 and tests/golden/README.md both warn about this exact error.

vectors.sourceQuote: £70 (£60 profit + £10 stake)
vectors.note: 10/1, £5 each-way, stated as 1/5 for places 1-3. Independent restatement of pub-ew-001 by a different source.

vectors.sourceQuote: 2nd or 3rd -> £15
vectors.note: Third place specifically — the LAST paid place on 3-place terms, so it pins the boundary.
Fourth place on 3-place terms — one outside the boundary. Pairs with pub-ew-007 to pin it from both sides.

vectors.sourceQuote: £10 each-way (£20 total stake) ... Total return: £140 from a £20 outlay
vectors.note: Source states 12 runners. Its returns imply a 1/5 place fraction, so this only holds for a NON-HANDICAP 12-runner race — a handicap of that size pays 1/4 and would return £145. isHandicap is set false accordingly. This source is the lone dissenter on handicap 12-15 (docs/05 §4); the fixture is written to the consensus reading, not to its table.

vectors.sourceQuote: Total return: £30 from a £20 outlay
£10 each-way (£20 total) ... Total return: £56
vectors.note: Short-priced each-way. The place fraction produces 3/5 — a non-integer fractional price, which is where naive rounding shows up.

vectors.sourceQuote: Return of £16 from £20 stake. You've lost £4 even though the horse placed.
vectors.note: A PLACED bet that still loses money. The engine must return 1600 and report the bet as PARTIAL, not as a loss — status and P&L are different questions.

vectors.sourceQuote: Win portion: £5 x 40/1 = £200 + £5 stake = £205 / Place portion: £5 x 8/1 (one-fifth of 40/1) = £40 + £5 stake = £45 / Total return: £250
vectors.note: Long price. States the place fraction arithmetic explicitly — one-fifth of 40/1 is 8/1.

vectors.sourceQuote: Win portion: £5 x 40/1 = £200 + £5 stake = £205
5/1 = £5 return
vectors.note: £2.50 each-way, place part only, 1/5 terms. One-fifth of 5/1 is evens.
Non-integer stake (£2.50) at 1/5 of 20/1 = 4/1. Exercises pence-level rounding.
Longest price harvested. One-fifth of 100/1 is 20/1.

vectors.sourceQuote: Consider a £10 win bet at 6/1 in a two-horse dead heat. Your £10 stake becomes two £5 portions. One £5 wins at 6/1, returning £35 (£30 profit plus £5 stake). The other £5 is lost. Your total return is £35 from a £10 investment - £25 profit rather than the £60 profit you'd have received from an outright win.
vectors.note: TWO-WAY DEAD HEAT. Confirms tests/golden/README.md worked example 2: the stake is divided, the odds are not.

vectors.sourceQuote: That same £10 at 6/1 becomes three £3.33 portions. Only one-third wins: £3.33 x 7.00 = £23.31. From your £10 stake, you receive £23.31 back - a modest profit rather than the life-changing win you might have anticipated.
vectors.expectedDisputedReason: The source rounds the divided stake to £3.33 BEFORE multiplying by the odds. Rounding once at the end, as .claude/rules/money.md requires, gives £23.33 and not £23.31. A correct engine will FAIL this fixture by 2p. It is recorded because the disagreement is the point: it is a live question about whether intermediate rounding is the industry convention, and no bookmaker source was reachable to settle it. DO NOT treat as a passing target.
